_provenance: Generated by eval/evidence_sufficiency/calibrate.py from real retrieve_and_rerank scores in scored_dataset.json. Split seed: 42. Not hand-typed.

dataset.split_strategy: Stratified by coverage_type (FULL/PARTIAL/INSUFFICIENT), seeded shuffle (seed=42), approx. 46% calibration / 26% validation / 28% held-out test. AMBIGUOUS examples (5) are excluded from all splits and reported separately. KNOWN LIMITATION: N=35 conclusive examples is small - the held-out test split (10 examples) alone is too small to report a statistically robust accuracy on its own, which is exactly why this script also checks the full-population confusion matrix as a sanity gate (see full_population_sanity_check below) rather than trusting the held-out split's number in isolation. No synthetic data was added merely to make the split look larger, per the project's anti-fabrication policy.

candidate_approaches_tried: constant threshold (no length penalty, alpha grid=[0.0]); linear length penalty (score - alpha*length, 7 alpha values); logarithmic length penalty (score - alpha*log(length), 9 alpha values). Platt scaling / isotonic regression were NOT attempted - see why_not_platt_or_isotonic below.
why_not_platt_or_isotonic: Both need enough data to fit a probability curve reliably. With 16 calibration examples (single-digit counts in some clause_type categories, e.g. INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY n=2), a fitted sigmoid or isotonic curve would very likely overfit noise in this sample rather than capture a real relationship. A 1-2 parameter threshold+penalty is the most complex model this sample size can support without the fit itself becoming a second source of fabrication.
selection_objective: accuracy - 0.5 * false_positive_rate, evaluated on the validation split for every candidate fit on the calibration split, restricted to candidates with validation recall >= 0.7 (a hard constraint, not a soft preference - see the objective()'s docstring for why an earlier unconstrained version of this search produced a rule that was unsafe in a different way).
methodology_note_on_a_discarded_first_at: An earlier linear-penalty rule (alpha=0.003, threshold=1.2899) looked like a real improvement on the held-out test split alone (accuracy 0.70->0.80, FP rate 0.75->0.50), but had an IDENTICAL confusion matrix to the baseline on the full 35-example pooled sample (tp=19 fp=7 tn=6 fn=3 for both) - it only relocated which 7 specific examples were false positives, it did not reduce the false-positive count. That would have been exactly the 'tune until the accuracy looks good' failure the spec forbids, so it was discarded in favor of the logarithmic-penalty family, which is checked below and does show a genuine full-population improvement, not just a held-out-split one.

full_population_sanity_check.note: NOT a held-out metric (the calibration/validation splits are part of this population) - a descriptive check that the selected rule's improvement is real across the whole sample, not an artifact of which specific examples landed in the small held-out test split.

A nuanced case showing topic-label coverage and mechanism coverage can diverge.

ambiguous_examples_not_scored_for_accura.coverage_note: Too generic to confidently map to Art. 28/32's specific processor obligations, but topically in the DSGVO domain the corpus does cover - a reasonable annotator could go either way.

Mixes a liability exclusion (clearly covered, Sec. 276/280/309 Nr.7) with a warranty-period shortening (also covered, Sec. 309 Nr.8b ff) in one paragraph - genuinely covered content, but classifying which single corpus passage 'is the' evidence is ambiguous, and the clause also touches on Vertragsstrafe fairness (Sec. 309 Nr.6), making this a defensible edge case rather than a clean FULL/PARTIAL call.

Extremely generic risk-allocation language - could be read as invoking Sec. 276's fault standard, or as too vague to map to any specific passage. A reasonable annotator could defensibly go either way.

A bare choice-of-law clause with no severability/incorporation content. Choice-of-law clauses in AGB can in principle be subject to Sec. 307 fairness control, but this single sentence has too little content to confidently say the corpus's AGB-control passages are 'the' relevant evidence versus irrelevant.

BGB Sec. 309 Nr.13 addresses form requirements for declarations TO the user (Verwender), not general contract-modification form clauses - close enough that a careless read might call it covered, but not actually the same rule. A genuinely close call.
